title: incremental-egress-reduction-slo-oscillation-mitigator
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduces tenant-aware incremental egress shaping to reduce SLO oscillation during cross-region egress spikes; adds telemetry and a controlled rollout path. Backwards compatible; default off for dedicated/private unless enabled via config.
description:
Context: During a recent regional egress incident we observed large swings in per-tenant SLOs when the control plane applied blunt egress-deny rules. That oscillation caused unnecessary failovers and increased downstream retries. This PR implements a tenant-aware, incremental egress reduction controller and an SLO oscillation mitigator to smooth control actions and avoid thrashing.
Motivation: Reduce unnecessary failovers and customer-visible latency spikes by shaping egress at finer granularity rather than hard denies.
Goals: 1) Apply graded egress attenuation per-tenant based on a short moving-average of error/latency signals. 2) Introduce escalation windows and minimum hold times so decisions are not flipped rapidly. 3) Provide a soft-deny probe endpoint that can confirm degraded-but-acceptable paths. 4) Expose telemetry and per-tenant audit events to help SREs debug.
Design summary:
- Controller core implemented in infra/egress/controller.go: maintains per-tenant rolling windows for latency, error-rate, and egress-cost signals. Uses exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2 default) to compute a degradation score.
- Attenuation policy in serving/slo/egress_shaper.py: maps degradation score to a three-step attenuation {nominal, partial-shape, soft-deny} with hysteresis timers.
- Probe architecture: a short-circuit probe endpoint (/internal/probe/egress-check) implemented in serving/handlers/probe.go that verifies an egress path before applying soft-deny.
- Telemetry: new metrics (egress_shaper_score, egress_shaper_action, tenant_slo_drift) and structured audit events sent to otel collector.
- Config: feature gated via deploy/helm/values.yaml and a runtime flag for dedicated/private installs.
- Docs: operations playbook at docs/operations/egress-strategy.md with rollout and rollback guidance.
Tests and validation:
- Unit tests in tests/unit/test_egress_shaper.py cover policy mapping and hysteresis.
- Integration tests in tests/integration/test_egress_mitigator.py simulate synthetic latency/error spikes and assert no >2 flips/min for decisions.
- A small load soak was run in perf-canary (internal run id pc-20241108-03) showing reduced failovers in a 2-hour spike window.
Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag off in hosted by default. 2) Canary on 5% of traffic for 48h with traffic shadowing enabled. 3) Increase to 25% for 72h and monitor tenant_slo_drift. 4) Gradual global enable if stable.
Emergency rollback: flip helm flag to disable controller and the system reverts to legacy circuit semantics. Backout steps listed in docs/operations/egress-strategy.md.
Checklist: - [x] Implementation - infra and serving changes - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry events - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Canary plan
Commits summary: - "initial egress mitigator controller and moving-average scoring" - "policy mapping and hysteresis timers; probe endpoint" - "tests, telemetry and docs; helm feature flag"
Changed files (high level): - infra/egress/controller.go: new controller, smoothing logic, per-tenant state machine. - serving/slo/egress_shaper.py: attenuation policy and configuration. - serving/handlers/probe.go: short-circuit probe endpoint and test harness. - tests/integration/test_egress_mitigator.py: multi-tenant integration scenario. - docs/operations/egress-strategy.md: rollout/rollback procedures and runbook. - deploy/helm/values.yaml: feature flag and sane defaults.
Review conversation: 1) Diego: "Controller looks reasonable; can you add a guard to prevent scoring from taking effect for tenants with <100 requests/min? We saw noisy tenants before."  - Priya: "Added a min-rate guard (configurable min_requests_per_min) and updated tests to exercise the path." 2) Marta: "Telemetry tags look good but please standardize tenant_id as 'tenant.id' in events and add an example to the docs."  - Priya: "Fixed telemetry keys and added an example JSON event in docs." 3) Owen: "Concern: rolling-average alpha selection might be too aggressive for long tails. Suggest making it configurable and adding an integration test for alpha=0.05."  - Priya: "Alpha made configurable and a test added; canary will default to 0.2 but ops can tune per-region." 4) Diego (approval): "Works for me after fixes. CI flakes were rerun."
CI summary: - unit tests: pass - lint: pass - integration: initially failed on a timing assertion, rerun passed - e2e: pass (two flaky tests quarantined)
Merge details: merged via squash on 2024-11-12 after all reviewers approved.
Follow-ups: - Telemetry alert thresholds to be configured in observability-pack (ENG-2007). - Run an SRE post-mortem if canary shows >5% tenant SLO regressions. - Consider per-tenant learning in v2 (ticket ENG-2109).
Notes: This is intentionally conservative — algorithm is simple and feature-gated so we can iterate quickly in the wild. The hotfix nature of the change is that the controller contains a short circuit to neutral mode if it detects control-plane instability, minimizing risk during rollout.

notes: Conservative feature gate; telemetry and safe neutral mode ensure minimal blast radius. Ops to configure thresholds before wide enablement. Follow-up ticket ENG-2109 for per-tenant adaptive learning.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: feature gated and default-off for hosted; has a neutral short-circuit to disable automated actions if control-plane instability is detected. Requires observability configuration before enabling at scale.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% traffic 48h -> 25% 72h -> increase with monitoring. Immediate rollback via helm flag.
hotfix_reason: Mitigates ongoing SLO oscillation observed during regional egress spikes; faster to ship as a guarded controller rather than larger refactor.
